title: Signaling role of phytohormone 6-Benzylaminopurine in augmenting saline wastewater bio-treatment performance and underlying mechanisms
description: This study introduced the phytohormone 6-benzylaminopurine (6-BA) as a novel, economical, and eco-friendly bacterial signal molecule (SM), overcoming the cost and instability limitations of acyl-homoserine lactones (AHLs) in high-salinity wastewater treatment. Against high-salinity stress, 6-BA promoted cellular integrity and ionic homeostasis, increasing live-cell counts by 113.7%. To mitigate phenol toxicity, 6-BA reinforced extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) functions and antioxidant systems to reduce reactive oxygen species (ROS) by 19.8%. 6-BA up-regulated the expression of DNA replication, TCA cycle, and fatty-acid synthesis pathways repairing membrane integrity. Simultaneously, 6-BA enriched the expression of degrading enzymes, enhanced phenol degradation, while COD, TN, and TP removals rose by approximately 20%. Crucially, 6-BA-induced community restructuring reduced antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) host abundance by 27.9% and decreased ARG-encoding plasmids by 32.8%, curtailing horizontal-gene-transfer (HGT) risks. Concurrently, 6-BA exhibited no observable ecotoxicity. This study proposed 6-BA signaling as a novel bioaugmentation strategy to enhance remediation in high-salinity wastewater bio-treatment.
